page: Amazon Web Services trn1.32xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, purpose-engineered for deep learning training and large-scale model execution. It is powered by an x86_64 host system equipped with dual Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz, delivering 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading support. Host memory comprises 512.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of system memory per vCPU core. The primary computing acceleration stems from 16 AWS Trainium accelerators providing a collective 512 GB of high-bandwidth device VRAM. Integrated hardware includes 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 800 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel computing and aggregate host performance. The system achieves a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 86,301.41 alongside a strong multi-core score of 123,833.48 in stress-ng and 16,220.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Single-thread results remain average across benchmarks, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 1685.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1893.4. Cryptographic capabilities rank in the top 10% on PassMark at 109,511.98 due to dedicated hardware acceleration flags such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The host's DDR4 memory subsystem exhibits strong read throughput under cached conditions at 6,667.57 GB/sec, moderating to 334.77 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and a 2,662.38 overall PassMark memory score.

Data transmission and storage subsystems support massive ingestion pipelines, reinforced by 800 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and 7.6 TB of high-speed local NVMe storage. In multi-threaded in-memory benchmarks, trn1.32xlarge recorded strong throughput, reaching 103.85 million Redis SET operations per second and 69.41 GB/sec in static web serving. For LLM tasks, prompt processing demonstrates strong throughput across smaller and mid-sized architectures, sustaining 2,985.55 tokens/sec on 135M models and 189.43 tokens/sec on 7B models. Text generation scaling tapers on larger architectures, dropping to 2.78 tokens/sec on 70B models, illustrating the architecture's primary alignment with parallelized distributed training rather than standalone large-model autoregressive generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware layout provides an alternative to traditional GPU clusters by leveraging native AWS Trainium silicon bundled with dense NVMe storage and high-bandwidth interconnects. trn1.32xlarge is best suited for distributed deep learning model pre-training, large-scale transformer fine-tuning, high-throughput batch inference pipelines, and parallelized machine learning workloads requiring substantial local cache storage and high-bandwidth node-to-node synchronization.
description: Amazon Web Services trn1.32xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring 16 integrated AWS Trainium accelerators with 512 GB of aggregate device VRAM. The host compute environment provides 128 vCPUs (64 physical cores) via an Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, supported by 512.0 GB of DDR4 system memory. Bundled storage includes 7600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD space alongside an 800 Gbps network interface. Benchmark results highlight top-tier cryptographic and multi-core CPU capacity, coupled with strong prompt processing speeds for small to mid-size language models, though single-core metrics and 70B autoregressive generation speeds remain modest. Designed as a cost-efficient deep learning architecture, trn1.32xlarge is targeted at distributed model training, transformer fine-tuning, large-scale batch inference, and compute-heavy parallel workloads.
